oewn-10308837-n.learner: a man who works under another person and takes orders from them
examples: The boss sent two of his men to collect the money.

oewn-10308424-n.learner: a grown male who has a manly character: strong, brave and able to do things well
examples: Two years at sea made a man of him.

connotation.why: praises a male as properly strong and brave, not just adult

oewn-02475618-n.learner: all of the people who are living on the earth.
examples: The disease was a danger to man in every country on earth.

connotation.why: a male word standing for all living people

oewn-87754171-n.learner: a man who serves in the armed forces; a member of a fighting force
examples: Five thousand men were killed in the battle.

oewn-02474924-n.learner: any member, living or extinct, of the human family of animals, marked by great intelligence, clear speech and walking upright.
examples: Early man made simple tools from stone.

connotation.why: a male word standing for the whole human kind

oewn-03721866-n.learner: an object used as a playing piece in certain board games
examples: She set up the men on the chessboard before her father came in.

oewn-10765000-n.learner: a male servant whose job is to look after his employer in person
examples: His man laid out his clothes for dinner.

oewn-02111896-v.learner: to get a message or other news from someone
examples: We have not heard from her since she moved away.

oewn-02506551-v.learner: to examine or listen to evidence or a case as part of a court's legal process
examples: The judge will hear the case next week.

oewn-10697152-n.learner: a person who supports a politician, a team, or something similar
examples: The senator has many friends in the farming towns who vote for him every time.

oewn-10352574-n.learner: a name used when speaking to a mother superior, the woman who is head of a convent
examples: Every nun in the convent addressed the abbess as mother.

oewn-15131241-n.learner: a stringy, slimy substance made of yeast and bacteria that forms when something ferments, and is added to cider or wine to turn it into vinegar
examples: Add a spoonful of mother to the cider to start the vinegar.

oewn-05798457-n.learner: the word as used in a formal set phrase
examples: The minister holds office at the pleasure of the king.
He took his pleasure and left before dawn.

oewn-05658424-n.learner: the ability or power of the mind to stay fixed on something
examples: Lack of sleep weakens your attention.

oewn-00656128-n.learner: the work of giving treatment to someone or something, or of looking after them
examples: The wounded soldiers needed medical attention.

oewn-05089997-n.learner: a way of standing still and straight with your arms at your sides and your feet together, used by soldiers during drill or inspection
examples: The soldiers stood at attention while the general passed.

oewn-01916886-v.learner: to go along or across a place or distance on foot
examples: We walked the whole length of the beach.

oewn-01910816-v.learner: to make someone or something walk
examples: She walks the dog every morning.

oewn-02524505-v.learner: to live or behave in a particular way
examples: For years they walked in fear of the secret police.

oewn-02475941-v.learner: to be joined with someone, or to act together with them
examples: She chose to walk with the poor all her life.

oewn-01963635-v.learner: to move along at a walking pace
examples: Let the horse walk for a while before you trot again.

oewn-01115898-v.learner: in baseball, to get to first base because the pitcher has thrown four balls
examples: The batter walked in the ninth inning.

oewn-01143080-v.learner: in baseball, to let a batter go to first base by throwing four balls
examples: The pitcher walked two batters in a row.

oewn-00718436-v.learner: to treat something as already true, or to assume it in advance
examples: Your question supposes that I was there, but I was not.

oewn-00718250-v.learner: to need something to be true or to happen first, as a condition
examples: Winning a race supposes that you entered it.

oewn-01694952-v.learner: to put words or symbols on a surface by marking or tracing them
examples: She wrote her name in the sand with a stick.

oewn-01703755-v.learner: to put down or say the letters that make up the usual form of a word or part of a word
examples: In Britain you write 'colour' with a u.

oewn-01709353-v.learner: to create music by writing it
examples: Mozart wrote his first symphony when he was eight.

oewn-01000931-v.learner: to record information on a computer
examples: The program writes the results to a file.

oewn-01696729-v.learner: to create code; to make a computer program
examples: She wrote a small program to sort the list.

oewn-00102205-r.learner: to a stage or point that is well along
examples: She is clever and will go far.

oewn-00101751-r.learner: a long way away in time
examples: These events lie far in the past.
